text: When a family has a gift card or credit with us, they shouldn't pay the whole bill by card. Use what they have first.
The Riveras owe one hundred sixty two dollars today.
Gift card and credit first. The card takes what's left.
Start with the gift card. Click Gift card.
Type the sixteen letter code from the card.
Click Check balance.
It has fifty dollars. Use all of it, or type a smaller amount.
Click Apply gift card.
Scout says how much it took, and what's left on the card.
And the bill shows fifty dollars paid.
Next, their account credit. Click Account credit.
Scout fills in what they have, up to what's owed.
Click Apply credit.
The credit is used, and the balance drops.
Now click Card on file. The card takes only what's left, eighty two dollars.
Wait for this note.
Three payments, one bill, all paid.
In Maria's ledger, the invoice shows all three payments.
To take part of a bill in cash or by check, use the ledger. Pick the method.
Then type the amount, and the cash received. Card payments always take the whole balance.

The most common mistakes are charging the full bill to the card when the family has credit, and forgetting a gift card they brought. Remember: apply the gift card and credit first. The card takes only what's left.
